q: Statements: A > B = C > D. Conclusions: I. A > D. II. B > D.
exp: A > B = C > D means A is greater than D and B is greater than D. Both conclusions follow.

q: Statements: P > Q > R > S. Conclusions: I. P > S. II. Q > S.
exp: From P > Q > R > S, P > S and Q > S are both directly implied.

q: Statements: M < N = O < P. Conclusions: I. M < P. II. N < P.
exp: M < N = O < P, so M < P and N < P. Both conclusions follow.

q: Statements: X > Y = Z < W. Conclusions: I. X > Z. II. W > Y.
exp: X > Y = Z, so X > Z. Also Z < W and Y = Z, so W > Y. Both follow.

q: Statements: A < B < C = D. Conclusions: I. A < D. II. B < D.
exp: Since A < B < C = D, both A < D and B < D are true.

q: Statements: L > M = N > O. Conclusions: I. L > O. II. M > O.
exp: L > M = N > O gives L > O and M > O. Hence both follow.

q: Statements: R = S > T > U. Conclusions: I. R > U. II. S > U.
exp: R = S and S > T > U, so both R > U and S > U follow.

q: Statements: H < I = J > K. Conclusions: I. H < J. II. I > K.
exp: H < I = J, so H < J. Also J > K and I = J, so I > K.

q: Statements: C > D < E. Conclusions: I. C > E. II. C > D.
exp: C > D is given. But the relation between C and E cannot be determined because both are greater than D.

q: Statements: F < G > H. Conclusions: I. F < H. II. G > F.
exp: G > F is given. The relation between F and H cannot be determined because both are less than G.

q: In a code, A @ B means A > B, A # B means A < B, and A $ B means A = B. If P @ Q # R, which conclusion follows?
exp: P > Q and Q < R do not establish a definite relation between P and R. Therefore it cannot be determined.

q: In a code, A @ B means A > B and A # B means A < B. If X @ Y @ Z, which is definitely true?
exp: X > Y and Y > Z, so X > Z.

q: In a code, P * Q means P < Q and P + Q means P = Q. If M * N + O, which conclusion is true?
exp: M < N and N = O, so M < O.

q: In a code, A @ B means A ≤ B, A # B means A ≥ B, and A $ B means A = B. If X # Y $ Z, what is the relation between X and Z?
exp: X ≥ Y and Y = Z, so X ≥ Z.

q: In a code, M @ N means M > N, N # P means N ≥ P, and P $ Q means P = Q. What can be concluded about M and Q?
exp: M > N and N ≥ P = Q. Therefore M > Q.

q: In a code, A % B means A < B and B & C means B = C. If P % Q & R, which conclusion follows?
exp: P < Q and Q = R, hence P < R.

q: In a code, A @ B means A > B, A # B means A < B, and A * B means A ≥ B. If P @ Q * R, what is definitely true?
exp: P > Q and Q ≥ R, so P > R.

q: Statements: A ≥ B > C = D. Conclusions: I. A > D. II. B > D.
exp: B > C = D, so B > D. Since A ≥ B > D, A > D also follows.

q: Statements: P ≤ Q = R < S. Conclusions: I. P < S. II. Q < S.
exp: Q = R < S, so Q < S. Since P ≤ Q < S, P < S. Both follow.

q: Statements: M > N ≥ O = P. Conclusions: I. M > P. II. N ≥ P.
exp: N ≥ O = P, so N ≥ P. Also M > N ≥ P, hence M > P. Both follow.

q: Statements: X ≤ Y < Z. Conclusions: I. X < Z. II. Y > X.
exp: X ≤ Y < Z guarantees X < Z. But X may equal Y, so Y > X is not certain.

q: Statements: A > B ≥ C > D. Conclusions: I. A > C. II. B > D.
exp: A > B ≥ C gives A > C. Also B ≥ C > D gives B > D. Both follow.

q: Statements: E < F ≤ G = H. Conclusions: I. E < H. II. F ≤ H.
exp: F ≤ G = H, so F ≤ H. Also E < F ≤ H, giving E < H. Both follow.

q: Statements: R ≥ S > T = U. Conclusions: I. R > U. II. S > U.
exp: S > T = U, so S > U. Since R ≥ S > U, R > U. Both follow.

q: Statements: K < L = M ≤ N. Conclusions: I. K < N. II. M ≤ N.
exp: K < L = M ≤ N gives K < N and M ≤ N. Both are true.

q: Statements: C ≥ D > E. Conclusions: I. C > E. II. C ≥ D.
exp: C ≥ D is given, and D > E means C > E. Both follow.

q: Statements: U < V ≤ W. Conclusions: I. U < W. II. V > U.
exp: U < V ≤ W gives U < W and V > U. Both follow.

q: Statements: B > C < D. Conclusions: I. B > D. II. D > C.
exp: D > C is given because C < D. The relation between B and D cannot be determined.

q: Statements: G < H > I. Conclusions: I. G < I. II. H > G.
exp: H > G is given. But G and I are both less than H, so their mutual relation is uncertain.

q: Statements: J > K < L. Conclusions: I. J > L. II. L > K.
exp: L > K is given. J and L may have any relation because both are greater than K.

q: Statements: S ≤ T = U. Conclusions: I. S ≤ U. II. U > S.
exp: Since T = U and S ≤ T, S ≤ U. U > S is not certain because S may equal U.

q: Statements: V ≥ W = X. Conclusions: I. V ≥ X. II. V > X.
exp: V ≥ W and W = X, so V ≥ X. But V may equal X, so V > X is not definite.

q: Statements: A = B < C ≤ D. Conclusions: I. A < D. II. B < D.
exp: A = B < C ≤ D, so both A < D and B < D are true.

q: Statements: P > Q = R ≥ S. Conclusions: I. P > S. II. Q ≥ S.
exp: Q = R ≥ S gives Q ≥ S. Since P > Q ≥ S, P > S. Both follow.

q: Statements: M < N ≥ O. Conclusions: I. M < O. II. N > M.
exp: N ≥ O and M < N. Thus N > M. The relation between M and O is uncertain.

q: Statements: X = Y > Z ≤ W. Conclusions: I. X > Z. II. Y > W.
exp: X = Y > Z, so X > Z. But Z ≤ W does not establish Y > W.

q: Statements: R < S = T ≥ U. Conclusions: I. R < U. II. S ≥ U.
exp: S = T ≥ U, so S ≥ U. The relation between R and U is uncertain.

q: Statements: A > B and C > D. What is the relationship between A and C?
exp: The two inequalities involve separate pairs, so no definite relationship between A and C can be established.

q: Statements: P > Q, R > S, and Q = R. What is the relationship between P and S?
exp: P > Q and Q = R > S. Therefore P > S.

q: Statements: A < B, B = C, and D < C. What is the relationship between A and D?
exp: A and D are both less than B/C, but their relation to each other is not fixed.

q: Statements: L > M, N = M, and O < N. What is the relationship between L and O?
exp: L > M = N > O, so L > O.

q: Statements: H ≤ I, I < J, and K = J. What is the relationship between H and K?
exp: H ≤ I < J = K, so H < K.

q: Statements: F ≥ G, G > H, and H = I. What is the relationship between F and I?
exp: F ≥ G > H = I. Therefore F > I.

q: Statements: A @ B means A > B, A # B means A < B, and A $ B means A = B. If P # Q $ R @ S, which conclusion is definitely true?
opts: Both P < R and Q > S
exp: P < Q = R and R > S, so P < R and R > S. Thus Q = R > S, so Q > S. Both P < R and Q > S are true.

q: In a coded inequality, A @ B means A ≤ B and A # B means A ≥ B. If X @ Y # Z, which relation between X and Z is possible?
opts: Any of X > Z, X = Z, or X < Z
exp: X ≤ Y and Y ≥ Z impose no fixed relationship between X and Z. All three possibilities are possible.

q: In a coded inequality, P * Q means P > Q, P / Q means P < Q, and P % Q means P = Q. If A * B % C / D, which conclusion definitely follows?
exp: A > B = C and C < D. Since A > C and C < D, A and D are not necessarily ordered.

q: Statements: A > B, C > D, and B = C. Conclusions: I. A > D. II. A > C.
exp: A > B = C > D, so A > D. A > C also follows because A > B and B = C.

q: Statements: P < Q, R < S, and Q = S. Conclusions: I. P < R. II. P < S.
exp: P < Q = S, so P < S. But P and R may have any relation, so I does not follow.

q: Statements: M ≥ N, N = O, and O > P. Conclusions: I. M > P. II. M ≥ O.
exp: M ≥ N = O > P, so M > P and M ≥ O. Both follow.

q: Statements: X < Y, Y ≤ Z, and Z = W. Conclusions: I. X < W. II. Y < W.
exp: X < Y ≤ Z = W gives X < W. Also Y ≤ W, but Y may equal W, so Y < W is not definite.

q: Statements: C = D ≥ E > F. Conclusions: I. C > F. II. D > F.
exp: D ≥ E > F gives D > F, and C = D means C > F. Both follow.

q: Statements: U > V ≥ W = X. Conclusions: I. U > X. II. V ≥ X.
exp: V ≥ W = X, so V ≥ X. Since U > V ≥ X, U > X. Both follow.

q: Statements: A ≤ B, C ≤ D, and B < C. Conclusions: I. A < D. II. A < C.
exp: A ≤ B < C ≤ D, so A < C and A < D. Both conclusions follow.
